description.narrative: Projektstödet till IOM fortsätter att stärka det ”Comprehensive Peace System” som man kom överens om i fredsavtalet 2016. Det tidigare bidraget avslutades i april 2024 med Sidas ID 10773. Målet med det nya programmet är att ”bidra till att garantera rättigheterna för offer för den colombianska väpnade konflikten av alla kön, åldrar, förmågor och andra olikheter, främja deras återhämtning och motståndskraft för stabilisering och fredsbyggande”. Programmets mål är följande: - De enheter som ingår i det övergripande fredssystemet garanterar offrens rättigheter genom att på ett hållbart sätt ta itu med drivkrafterna bakom våld och konflikt och därigenom bidra till nationell försoning. - Brottsoffer, civilsamhällesorganisationer och före detta kombattanter deltar aktivt i de utrymmen som inrättats genom fredsavtalet, inom det övergripande fredssystemet, för att främja deras gottgörelse och försoning.

The project support to IOM continues to strengthen of the “Comprehensive Peace System” that was agreed upon in the peace agreement of 2016. The previous contribution ended in April 2024 with Sida´s ID 10773. The objective of the new program is to “contribute to guaranteeing the rights of victims of the Colombian armed conflict of all genders, ages, abilities, and other diversities, promoting their recovery and resilience for stabilization and peacebuilding”. The program objectives are: - The entities comprising the Comprehensive Peace System guarantee the victims' rights by sustainably addressing the drivers of violence and conflict, thereby contributing to national reconciliation. - Victims, civil society organizations, and ex-combatants actively participate in the spaces established by the Peace Agreement, within the Comprehensive Peace System, to promote their reparation and reconciliation.

The overall objective of the intervention is to contribute to guaranteeing the rights of victims of the Colombian armed conflict of all genders, ages, abilities, and other diversities, promoting their recovery and resilience for stabilization and peacebuilding.
This will be achieved with the following outcomes:
1. The entities comprising the Comprehensive Peace System guarantee the rights of the victims by sustainably addressing the drivers of violence and conflict, thereby contributing to national reconciliation.
2. Victims, civil society organizations, and ex-combatants actively participate in the spaces established by the Peace Agreement, within the Comprehensive Peace System, to promote their reparation and reconciliation.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Since the beginning of the contribution, 25 projects have been supported, 20 of which are currently being implemented. The process of identifying the main priorities for the institutions that are part of the Comprehensive Peace System was very slow. This affected the financial execution of the contribution, as highlighted by the auditors in their reports to Sida and IOM.
Despite this initial setback, in 2025, IOM focused on identifying activities with the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (SJP), the Search Unit, and the Follow-up Committee for the Truth Commissions recommendations.
Nevertheless, some results have been achieved by the contribution during this year and half of implementation.
- Adjustment of the Truth Commission's "Hay Futuro si Hay Verdad" exhibition for smaller venues. This adaptation will enable the Ministry of Culture to take the exhibition to different cities, with a focus on those that were more affected by the armed conflict.
- Identification of 35 places of forensic interest with the potential to contain the remains of more than 175 missing persons, based on information obtained from perpetrators. With this result, the indicator about the number of forensic places identified was exceeded by 300%.
- Technical support for advancing the investigations into gender-based violence as part of macro-case 11. Thanks to Sida's contribution, the three sub-cases have received input for the systematization and identification of potential restorative activities.
- For the first time in history, the UN Team of Experts on Sexual Violence will work in Colombia supporting the SJP in investigating gender-based violence according to international standards. Sixty-one former military personnel involved in human rights violations and their lawyers received training to incorporate a restorative approach into their participation in judicial activities and dialogue with victims. As a result, a restorative dialogue was held in Comuna 13 in Medellín.
The contribution yielded some unexpected results concerning the utilisation of resources from public investments. In some of the 25 projects, Swedish resources were used as a financial contribution by IOM to increase the impact by implementing memory and articulation initiatives for the implementation of SJP sanctions and reparation for victims in collaboration with public institutions. Financed by the Mayor of Bogotá and the Ministry of the Interior, these initiatives align with the purpose of the contribution and leveraged an amount of SEK 43,000,000.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
